correlations.title: Risk Correlation Matrix
correlations.clickHint: Click a cell in the upper triangle to edit a pair.
correlations.conceptHelp: How much two risks move together. Positive means they rise and fall together, amplifying tail losses; negative means one offsets the other. The Monte Carlo simulation samples correlated draws so portfolio VaR reflects this.
correlations.psdHelp: A valid correlation matrix must be positive semi-definite — otherwise the coefficients are mutually contradictory and the simulation cannot sample from them. Auto-suggest keeps it valid.
correlations.nonPsdWarning: This matrix is not positive semi-definite, so it will be dropped from Monte Carlo simulations (risks sampled independently). Adjust the coefficients until the matrix is valid.
correlations.notPdWarning: This matrix is positive semi-definite but not strictly positive-definite (smallest eigenvalue ≈ 0 — usually a ±1.0 or otherwise dependent coefficient). The Monte Carlo needs strict positive-definiteness for its Cholesky step, so it will drop these correlations and sample risks independently until you adjust them.

stopMethods.heading: Three ways to stop this agent
stopMethods.reasonYes: A reason is required, and the server refuses a blank one.
stopMethods.suspendInFlight: Refuses the next request. A run already under way continues to the end.
stopMethods.suspendNote: Its credentials are refused at registration while it is suspended.
stopMethods.suspendNoteUnenforced: This workspace does not enforce agent registration, so suspending does not refuse anything. It also WIDENS what the agent may reach: an inactive agent bypasses its tool allowlist, its autonomy cap and its policy card. Use the kill switch instead.
stopMethods.killInFlight: Checked on every tool call, so a run already under way stops at its next tool call.
stopMethods.killUndo: Reversible: lifting it is a separate deliberate act.
stopMethods.killNote: Can stop this agent alone or every agent in the workspace. It does not change the agent's status, so the register still reads ACTIVE.
stopMethods.retireInFlight: Refuses the next request, and revokes the API keys bound to the agent, which are re-checked on every tool call.
stopMethods.retireUndo: PERMANENT. It cannot be undone and the agent cannot be brought back into service.
stopMethods.retireNote: Also drops its tool grants, expires its proposals still awaiting review and freezes its policy card.

autonomy.rung0: Suggests to a human in session and reaches nothing itself. No tool sits at this rung, so an agent registered here can call nothing.

autonomy.rungAboveTop: No capability requires this rung today, so it grants nothing beyond orchestrate. Registering an agent here does not widen what it can reach.
autonomy.effectiveNote: What an agent may actually do is the LOWEST of this rung, its credential's ceiling, and the cap its assessed risk tier allows. An unassessed agent is refused everything, whatever this says.

blocked.permission: Connecting an agent creates an API key, which needs the permission to manage API keys. Ask an owner or an admin.
blocked.grantsUnreadable: The key's scopes come from this agent's granted tools, and you cannot read them. Ask an owner or an admin.
blocked.inactive: Only an active agent can be connected. Activate the agent first.
blocked.grantsEmpty: This agent is granted no tools, so a key for it could call nothing. Grant tools on the Tools tab first.

amend.title: Amend {name}
amend.name: Name
amend.loweringAlwaysAllowed: Lowering autonomy is always permitted and needs no re-assessment. Raising it is capped by the agent's assessed risk tier.
amend.ownerMovesByTransfer: Ownership moves only by a two-step transfer: another holder of the tenant lifecycle permission proposes it, and the person it names accepts it.

overview.credentialsValue: {count, plural, one {# live API key} other {# live API keys}}

stateBody.DRAFT: This agent has never been put into service. Its credentials are refused at registration until someone activates it.
stateBody.ACTIVE: This agent's credentials are accepted at registration. Suspending it refuses them from the next request onward.
stateBody.SUSPENDED: This agent is suspended in the register, so its credentials are refused at registration. It stays in the register and can be activated again.
stateBody.RETIRED: This agent is retired, so its credentials are refused at registration. Retirement is permanent: it revokes the API keys bound to the agent, drops its tool grants, expires its proposals still awaiting review and freezes its policy card. The register keeps its record and the authority it held.

overview.activateError: The agent could not be activated.
overview.suspendPrompt: Suspension is reversible, and the register keeps the record of it.
overview.suspendScope: The agent's credentials are refused at the next registration request. A run already under way is not affected.
overview.suspendCredentials: {count, plural, one {# API key bound to this agent is live — neither revoked nor expired.} other {# API keys bound to this agent are live — neither revoked nor expired.}}
overview.suspendError: The agent could not be suspended.
overview.unscoredBody: An unassessed agent is refused every tool at the boundary, so it cannot be activated. Score it on the Risk assessment tab first.
overview.legacyBody: This row adopts proposals made before the register existed. It is not a real agent, and changing its availability changes nothing that runs.
overview.readOnly: Changing this agent's availability needs permission to manage the agent register.
overview.loadErrorTitle: This agent could not be loaded
overview.loadErrorBody: The register could not be read. Nothing about the agent has changed.
overview.forbiddenBody: You do not have permission to read this agent's register entry. Contact your workspace administrator to request access.
overview.suspendCredentialsNone: No API key bound to this agent is still live, so suspending it changes nothing that runs today
overview.notFoundTitle: This agent is no longer in the register
overview.notFoundBody: The register answered, and it holds no entry with this id. It was most likely removed after this page opened. Reload to see the register as it stands.
overview.staleBody: The register could not be re-read just now, so these figures may be out of date. They refresh on the next successful read.
overview.suspendScopeUnenforced: This workspace does not require registered agents, so the agent's credentials are still accepted at registration — but a suspended agent is refused every tool call at the boundary, and its granted tools, its autonomy ceiling, its policy card and its stop controls apply again. Reading the framework catalogue is not refused, and neither is anything the key's own scope allows outside the agent surface. A run already under way is not affected.

stateBodyUnenforced.DRAFT: This agent has never been put into service. This workspace does not require registered agents, so a credential bound to it is accepted anyway — and because the agent is not active it never resolves at the tool boundary, so its granted tools, its autonomy ceiling and its policy card do not apply to that credential.
stateBodyUnenforced.ACTIVE: This agent's credentials are accepted at registration. This workspace does not require registered agents, so they would be accepted whatever the register said about this agent — but while it is active, its granted tools, its autonomy ceiling and its policy card do apply to them at the tool boundary.
stateBodyUnenforced.SUSPENDED: This agent is suspended in the register. This workspace does not require registered agents, so its credentials are still accepted at registration — but while it is suspended every tool call is refused at the boundary, and its granted tools, its autonomy ceiling, its policy card and its stop controls apply again. It can still read the framework catalogue. It stays in the register and can be activated again.
stateBodyUnenforced.RETIRED: This agent is retired. This workspace does not require registered agents, so it is retirement's own effects that stop it: retirement revokes the API keys bound to the agent and drops its tool grants. A credential bound to it that is still live is accepted at registration, and this agent's granted tools, autonomy ceiling and policy card do not apply to it. The register keeps its record and the authority it held.

overview.retirePrompt: Retirement is permanent. It cannot be undone, and the agent cannot be brought back into service.
overview.retireCascadeIntro: Retiring this agent does all of this at once:
overview.retireCascadeKeys: {count, plural, one {# live API key bound to it is revoked.} other {# live API keys bound to it are revoked.}}
overview.retireCascadeKeysNone: No live API key is bound to it.
overview.retireCascadeTools: {count, plural, one {# tool grant is dropped.} other {# tool grants are dropped.}}
overview.retireCascadeProposals: {count, plural, one {# proposal awaiting review expires, and can no longer be approved.} other {# proposals awaiting review expire, and can no longer be approved.}}
overview.retireCascadeProposalsNone: None of its proposals is awaiting review.
overview.retireCascadeCard: Its policy card is frozen: no further version can be written, and its history stays readable.
overview.retireIrreversible: Suspension stops this agent just as completely and can be lifted. Retirement cannot.

risk.neverScoredTitle: This agent has never been assessed
risk.neverScoredBody: No completed run means no tier, and no tier is refused at the tool boundary rather than read as low risk. Answer the questions below, then complete the run to score it.
risk.tierInForceDiffers: This run scored {scored}, but {inForce} is what caps the agent today. An axis widened since, and the tier was recomputed from these same answers — the cap only ever tightens.
risk.stalenessUnknownBody: This run recorded no basis to compare the agent against, so there is nothing to check it for drift. Treat it as unverified, not as current.
risk.freshBody: Nothing the scorer reads has moved in the risk-raising direction since this run was completed.
risk.staleTitle: The agent has moved since this run
risk.staleBody: The answers may be out of date. The tier itself is not left behind — a widening is re-scored from these same answers in the transaction that records it — so this is a prompt to re-answer, not an outage.
risk.staleSinceBody: Stale since {when}. The answers may be out of date. The tier itself is not left behind — a widening is re-scored from these same answers in the transaction that records it — so this is a prompt to re-answer, not an outage.
risk.unansweredCountAsNo: {count, plural, one {# applicable question has no answer} other {# applicable questions have no answer}}. Completing now scores each of them as No.
risk.allNotApplicable: Every question is marked N/A. The scorer reads an empty denominator as nothing demonstrated, so this costs the full answer weight rather than saving it.
risk.completeHint: Writes a risk tier onto the agent. The run cannot be reopened afterwards.
risk.confirmPrompt: Scoring writes a risk tier onto the agent in one transaction. From then on that tier caps how far the agent may be driven on every tool call.
risk.confirmUnanswered: {count} of {applicable} applicable questions have no answer. Each one is scored as No — an unclaimed mitigation counts as an absent one.
risk.confirmNeverReopened: A completed run is never reopened. Re-scoring later opens a new run, so this one stays as the record of the judgement made today.
risk.completeError: The assessment could not be completed.
risk.scoredBand: The additive score alone put it at {band}.
risk.scoredFloors: The additive score alone put it at {band}; raised by {floors}.
risk.scoredNoEvidence: No evidence artefact was filed for this run.
risk.saveError: The answer could not be saved.
risk.readOnlyBody: You can read this assessment but not change it. Answering questions and scoring the agent both need permission to change the agent register.
risk.forbiddenDescription: You do not have permission to read this agent's risk assessment. Contact your workspace administrator to request access.
risk.loadErrorTitle: The risk assessment could not be loaded
risk.loadErrorDescription: Neither the questionnaire nor the standing tier could be read. Nothing has been changed.
risk.noQuestionsDescription: The shared question set has not been loaded into this environment. An administrator can run the reference-data seed to install it.
risk.staleNoRescoreBody: The answers may be out of date, and the tier was NOT recomputed. Neither the granted-tool count nor the model reference is an input the scorer reads, so nothing re-ran and the cap has not tightened — re-answering the questions is the only thing that moves it.
risk.staleNoRescoreSinceBody: Stale since {when}. The answers may be out of date, and the tier was NOT recomputed. Neither the granted-tool count nor the model reference is an input the scorer reads, so nothing re-ran and the cap has not tightened — re-answering the questions is the only thing that moves it.
risk.staleToolCapNote: The grant itself is bounded instead: a tool whose autonomy rung sits above the standing tier's cap is refused at the moment it is granted.
risk.newRunBody: A completed run is never reopened, so opening this tab started a fresh draft. The standing assessment above is a separate, completed run and keeps its own answers — nothing was lost, and these blanks belong to the new run.
risk.ungroupedDescription: These questions name a dimension this response did not describe. They are counted in the totals above, so they are shown here rather than left with nowhere to answer them.

policyCard.heading: Policy card
policyCard.forbiddenDescription: You do not have permission to read or change this agent's policy card. Contact your workspace administrator to request access.
policyCard.loadErrorTitle: The policy card could not be loaded
policyCard.loadErrorDescription: The request failed before the card could be read. Nothing has been changed.
policyCard.seedIntro: A card is seeded from what is already true: the tools this agent has been granted, the data scope it is registered as reaching, and the autonomy cap and action budgets its assessed tier allows. Creating one changes nothing about what the agent may do — it pins it, and every later edit appends a version.
policyCard.seedHint: Version 1 is written from the register, not composed here.
policyCard.seedConfirmBody: Version 1 is written from the agent's current grants and its assessed tier, so nothing about what the agent may do changes today. There is no delete: every later change appends a version, and a card can only ever narrow what other layers already decided.
policyCard.seedError: The policy card could not be created.
policyCard.seedExistsError: This agent already has a policy card — somebody created one while this tab was open. The card below is the one in force.
policyCard.assessmentTitle: This agent has not been risk-assessed
policyCard.assessmentBody: The autonomy cap, the action budgets and the approval rung all come from the assessed tier, so there is nothing to seed a card from and every granted tool would be withheld. Complete the risk assessment first — a card of zeroes cannot be told apart from one somebody deliberately narrowed.
policyCard.withheldTitle: {count, plural, one {1 granted tool would be withheld} other {# granted tools would be withheld}}

withheldReason.NOT_IN_CATALOGUE: is not a tool this build offers
withheldReason.AUTONOMY_ABOVE_CARD: needs autonomy {requires}, and the card permits {permits}
withheldReason.DATA_SCOPE_ABOVE_CARD: reaches {requires} on every call, and the card stops at {permits}

policyCard.inForceMissingTitle: The version in force cannot be read
policyCard.inForceMissingBody: This card points at version {version} and that row is not there. Editing is refused until it is, because the ladder has nothing to measure a change against.
policyCard.historyIntro: Every edit appends a version and none is ever rewritten. This is the trail a run's pinned version is read against.
policyCard.historyCapped: Only the {count} most recent versions are listed.
policyCard.unchangedBody: This version declares exactly what the one before it declared.
policyCard.noVersionsDescription: A card is created together with its first version, so an empty history means the trail could not be read rather than that nothing has happened.
policyCard.editIntro: Narrowing is free — take as much away in one edit as you like. Widening is one rung, on one dimension, so each new reach is a decision somebody made rather than a line in a larger diff.
policyCard.widenSpent: This edit widens {dimension}. Every other widening is closed until it is saved — narrowing stays open everywhere.

ladderRefusal.MULTI_DIMENSION_WIDEN: This edit widens more than one dimension. Save the narrowings on their own, then widen one dimension.
ladderRefusal.MULTI_RUNG_WIDEN: This edit widens by more than one rung. Save it one rung short and repeat it — narrowing back down is always a single step.

policyCard.unexercisableTitle: This card would refuse a tool it permits
policyCard.toolsHint: The card narrows the grants: permitting a tool nobody granted grants nothing. A tool this card's own ceilings refuse on every call cannot be permitted at all.
policyCard.triggersHint: Dropping a trigger is a widening — the refusal still audits, but nothing wakes anybody.
policyCard.unchangedHint: Change something to save a new version
policyCard.saveError: The policy card could not be saved.
policyCard.conflictError: This card changed while your edit was in flight. Reload it and reapply your change.
policyCard.conflictErrorVersion: This card is now at version {version}; your edit was composed against an earlier one. Reload it and reapply your change — re-basing automatically would let two operators each widen by one rung and land two rungs from where either looked.
policyCard.missingCardError: This agent no longer has a policy card, so there is nothing to edit. The tab has been reloaded.
policyCard.writeForbidden: You do not have permission to change this agent's policy card.
policyCard.withheldIntro: The grant stands and nothing is revoked. A withheld tool is a disagreement between the grant and the agent's own declarations, and what would settle it depends on the ceiling it ran into.

withheldRemedy.NOT_IN_CATALOGUE: No ceiling permits it — this build does not carry the tool at all, so withdraw it rather than widen for it.
withheldRemedy.AUTONOMY_ABOVE_CARD: It becomes exercisable at autonomy {requires}, which the assessed tier has to allow first.
withheldRemedy.DATA_SCOPE_ABOVE_CARD: It becomes exercisable at {requires}, which the agent's registered data scope has to allow first.

policyCard.unexercisableIntro: This card permits tools its own ceilings refuse on every call, so saving is refused until each one is settled.
policyCard.historyWindowEdge: The versions before this one are not listed, so this row shows what it declares rather than what it moved.
policyCard.withheldNowTitle: {count, plural, one {1 granted tool is withheld} other {# granted tools are withheld}}
policyCard.withheldNowIntro: The grant stands and nothing is revoked, but every call to these tools is refused meanwhile. A withheld tool is a disagreement between the grant and the agent's own declarations, and what would settle it depends on the ceiling it ran into.
policyCard.autonomyCapHint: This agent's assessed risk tier ({tier}) caps autonomy at L{cap}, so no rung above it is offered: the tool boundary clamps every call to that cap, whatever the card says.
policyCard.dataScopeCapHint: This agent is registered as reaching {scope}. The card narrows that declaration and cannot widen past it, so no rung above it is offered — raise the agent's data-access scope first, which re-scores it on the spot.
policyCard.aboveTierCapTitle: This card reaches above the tier's autonomy cap
policyCard.aboveTierCapBody: The card declares L{card} and this agent's assessed risk tier ({tier}) caps autonomy at L{cap} — a re-assessment lowered the cap, and a stored version is never rewritten. Every call is already clamped to the cap, so narrowing the card here makes it say what is actually enforced. Every other change stays open meanwhile.
policyCard.aboveTierCapUnscoredBody: The card declares L{card} and this agent has not been risk-assessed, so its tier permits no autonomy at all and every call is already refused. Complete the risk assessment, or narrow the card to say what is actually enforced.
policyCard.aboveDeclaredScopeTitle: This card reaches past the data scope this agent is registered for
policyCard.aboveDeclaredScopeBody: The card reaches {card} and this agent is registered as reaching {scope} — the register was narrowed after this version was written, and a stored version is never rewritten. Nothing clamps this one: the tool boundary reads the card's rung and never the register's, so the wider reach is live on every call. Narrow the card to {scope}, or raise the agent's registered data-access scope if the wider reach is intended. Every other change stays open meanwhile.

tools.runtimeBody: These reach a Flue run whatever this agent was granted — the runtime adds them, not the register. Neither widens what the agent can reach today; each says below what bounds it. They are listed here because an operator reading the grants above was seeing a shorter list than the model is shown.
tools.widensRead: {tool} can READ this workspace's data. It cannot propose or change anything.
tools.widensPropose: {tool} can PROPOSE changes. Proposals land in the approval queue for a human — granting this does not let the agent commit anything on its own.
tools.widensBlocked: The tool boundary is refusing this tool right now because its definition changed and no one has accepted the new one. Granting it will have no effect until that pin is approved.
tools.heading: Granted tools
tools.intro: This agent can call only the tools listed here. Anything absent is refused at the tool boundary, however widely its credential is scoped.
tools.forbiddenBody: Granting an agent's tools is a separate permission from the agent register, and it covers reading the list as well as changing it. Ask a workspace administrator for it.
tools.retiredBody: The register does not list or change a retired agent's tools. Retirement is permanent, and it takes away what the agent may reach.
tools.loadFailedTitle: Tool grants could not be loaded
tools.loadFailedBody: The list of granted tools did not load, so this panel shows nothing rather than reporting an empty list as fact.
tools.noToolsDescription: Every tool call this agent makes is refused until one is granted.
tools.grantHint: Only tools this build defines can be granted. The agent's risk tier caps how far a tool may reach, and its declared data access bounds which tools it may hold at all.
tools.allGranted: Every tool in this build is already granted
tools.grantFailed: The tool could not be granted.
tools.grantForbidden: You do not have permission to change this agent's tools.
tools.revokeFailed: The tool could not be revoked.
tools.revokeForbidden: You do not have permission to change this agent's tools.
tools.inertHint: This grant names a tool the current build no longer defines, so nothing can call it. Revoking it clears the register.
tools.stalenessTitle: The risk assessment is now stale

manifests.heading: Tool definition pins
manifests.intro: A tool definition is a name, a parameter schema and a description — and the description is instruction text handed to the model on every call that no screen ever shows a person. A pin records the definition this workspace reviewed; the boundary refuses the tool while the build no longer matches it. These pins cover every agent here, not only this one.
manifests.forbiddenTitle: Tool definitions are not visible to you
manifests.forbiddenBody: Reading the definition pins needs the agent register permission.
manifests.loadFailedTitle: Tool definitions could not be loaded
manifests.loadFailedBody: The pin states did not load. Nothing here is a claim about whether a definition changed.
manifests.noDefinitionsDescription: This deployment defines no tools, so there is nothing to pin.

explain.APPROVED: The definition in this build is byte-identical to the one approved here.
explain.UNPINNED: Nothing is on file. The boundary met this definition first and let it through; approving it puts a named person behind it.
explain.DESCRIPTION_CHANGED: The instruction text the model reads has been rewritten since it was approved. The name and the parameters are untouched, so this change is visible nowhere except here.
explain.SCHEMA_CHANGED: The parameters changed. The instruction text the model reads is unchanged.
explain.DEFINITION_CHANGED: Both the parameters and the instruction text the model reads have changed since they were approved.

manifests.approveFailed: The definition could not be approved.
manifests.approveForbidden: Approving a tool definition needs the workspace administrator role, which is checked on top of the agent register permission. The definitions stay readable either way.
manifests.approveStale: The definition changed since this page read it. The digests shown have been refreshed — review them and approve again.
manifests.explainDefinitionOpaque: The definition digest differs, although neither the description nor the parameters changed. Nothing on this row explains the difference — treat it as a change until somebody can.
manifests.confirmTenantWide: This pin is TENANT-WIDE. Accepting it clears the boundary's refusal of this tool for every agent in the workspace at once — not just this one.
manifests.confirmDescriptionOnly: The DESCRIPTION changed and the schema did not. The description is instruction text delivered straight to the model, so this is the shape a tool-poisoning change takes: the structure looks identical and the behaviour is not. Read the text below before accepting.
manifests.confirmNoPriorText: Only hashes are pinned, so the previously approved wording is not retained and cannot be shown. What follows is the definition you are accepting, not a comparison.

tools.refusedTitle: The register would not list these tools
tools.blockedHint: The tool boundary is refusing this tool for every agent in this workspace, because its definition no longer matches the one approved here. The grant stands; the call does not get through until the definition is reviewed again below.
tools.blockedUnknown: Whether any of these tools is currently refused at the boundary could not be checked — the definition pins below did not load.
tools.stalenessCauseTool: This agent can now reach {toolName}, which it could not when it was last scored.
tools.stalenessCauseOther: This grant is not what made the assessment stale. Something else about this agent moved after it was scored, and the register found it while reconciling this change.
tools.stalenessRescored: The register re-scored the agent from {from} to {to} in the same step, so its autonomy ceiling has already tightened. Open the Risk assessment tab before assuming what this agent may still do.
tools.stalenessNoRescore: The assessed tier did not move in this step. The answers on file now describe a smaller agent than the one in the register, and only a fresh assessment settles that.

stalenessTrigger.TOOL_GRANTED: It holds more tools than it did when it was scored.
stalenessTrigger.DATA_SCOPE_WIDENED: Its declared data access was widened.
stalenessTrigger.REVERSIBILITY_WORSENED: Its actions became harder to undo.
stalenessTrigger.PROVENANCE_WIDENED: It now depends on a third-party supplier.

coverage.coveredOf: {covered} of {applicable} applicable agentic risks are covered for this agent
coverage.conservativeNote: A risk counts as covered only when it applies to this agent and a control is linked to it directly. Inherited coverage never counts towards this figure, and a control linked in this workspace is not evidence that it was tested against this agent.
coverage.gapsDescription: In scope for this agent with no control behind them. This is the list an assessor reads first.
coverage.reviewDescription: Reached only by a related cross-framework mapping. That is awareness, not a coverage claim — confirm each one by hand before relying on it.
coverage.partialDescription: Reached only through a cross-framework mapping. A mapping is Inflect's judgement that two obligations overlap, so it never counts as full coverage.
coverage.coveredDescription: Applies to this agent and linked directly to a control.
coverage.frameworkEmptyTitle: The installed framework carries no requirements
coverage.frameworkEmptyDescription: {framework} is installed but holds no requirement rows, so this agent cannot be assessed against it yet.
coverage.errorForbidden: You do not have permission to read this agent's risk coverage.
coverage.errorNotFound: This agent is no longer in the register.
coverage.errorLoad: The coverage report could not be loaded, so nothing is shown rather than a figure that might be wrong.

reason.noDirectControl: No control is linked directly to this risk
reason.notApplicable: The register shows this agent lacks the capability this risk names

coverage.notAvailableTitle: The OWASP ASI framework is not in this deployment's catalogue
coverage.notAvailableBody: Nothing here has been assessed against ASI01–ASI10, so there is no coverage figure to show. That is not the same as zero coverage — there is nothing yet to measure this agent against. The agentic-risk library is part of the product catalogue rather than a workspace setting, so it cannot be added from inside this workspace; an operator has to load it.
coverage.unrecognisedDescription: Inflect does not recognise the coverage status reported for these risks, so they are listed here rather than counted as covered or as a gap — neither reading is supported. Report this: it means the panel and the service disagree about what a status can be.
coverage.derivedScopeNote: Which risks apply is derived from this agent's own register entry — its tool grants and its autonomy level. Nobody has recorded an applicability decision for this agent, and the derivation changes the moment either column does.
coverage.applicableSplit: {notApplicable, plural, one {# risk does not apply to this agent and is not counted here} other {# risks do not apply to this agent and are not counted here}}
coverage.unassessedNotice: This agent has never been risk-assessed, so the register entry these figures are derived from is a declaration nobody has reviewed.
coverage.notApplicableDescription: This agent's register entry says it lacks the capability each of these risks names, and the platform enforces that lack server-side. It is derived from the register, not an applicability decision anyone recorded — grant this agent a tool or raise its autonomy level and the risk is back in scope, with no record that it ever was not.

basis.zeroToolGrants: This agent holds no tool grants, so it can call no tool. That is about the tool boundary only — it does not mean the agent touches nothing.
basis.suggestOnly: This agent is registered at autonomy 0 — it suggests only and takes no action of its own.

coverage.applicableSplitNone: Every risk in the framework applies to this agent

breaker.handClosed: This breaker was closed by hand on {at} as {reason}. The verdict below is the one that tripped it: it predates the close and is not a judgement that the behaviour resolved.

postureTitle.unobserved: Nothing has watched this agent yet
postureTitle.open: The breaker is open and this agent is stopped
postureTitle.armed: An anomalous window is on record
postureTitle.learning: Closed, but not judging anything yet
postureTitle.closedAfterTrip: Closed by hand after a trip — nothing judged since

postureBody.unobserved: There is no breaker record for this agent, so no window has ever been evaluated. This is not the same as a healthy breaker — a record appears the first time the agent calls a tool, and judging begins once it has {windows} active windows and {observations} tool calls behind it.
postureBody.open: Every tool call from this agent is refused at the boundary. Nothing closes the breaker on its own: there is no timeout, no trial call and no automatic recovery anywhere in this control. It stays open until an administrator closes it here.
postureBody.armed: One or more recent windows fired a signal. The breaker stops the agent only when the same signal fires in {required} consecutive active windows, so nothing is blocked yet.
postureBody.learning: A breaker record exists, but it has not seen enough of this agent's own history to call anything unusual. Windows are being recorded and none is being judged until there are {windows} active windows and {observations} tool calls.
postureBody.watching: Every completed window is compared against this agent's own history. No signal is firing and no streak is running.
postureBody.closedAfterTrip: An administrator closed this breaker after it tripped, so the agent is calling tools again. Nothing has judged it since — the last verdict on record is still that trip — and the next one is written the first time this agent calls a tool in a new hour. What that verdict is measured against depends on the reason the breaker was closed with, shown below.

breaker.streakExplain: The breaker trips only when the same signal fires in {required} consecutive active windows. A single odd window arms it and stops nothing.
breaker.guardBlocksExplain: The output guard refused these calls before they ran. {threshold} of them inside one hour latches the breaker at once — there is no streak and no baseline, because a blocked call has no normal to depart from. The count covers the hour still filling and starts again on the hour.
breaker.trippedSignalsUnrecorded: The record carries no signal codes for this trip, so what fired cannot be read from here. The window history below is the evidence that remains.
breaker.closeRestricted: Closing a breaker needs workspace-administrator rights on top of agent-register access. Ask an administrator to close it.
breaker.windowsCaption: The {count} most recent hourly windows, newest first.
breaker.noWindowsDescription: This agent has not called a tool since window recording began. The first window appears in the hour it does.
breaker.noBreakerDataDescription: The circuit-breaker endpoint returned nothing for this agent. Reload the page; if it stays empty, the agent may have been removed from the register.
breaker.loadErrorTitle: The circuit breaker could not be read
breaker.loadErrorBody: Nothing about the agent has changed — only this panel failed to load.
breaker.loadForbiddenBody: You do not have permission to read this agent's circuit breaker. Contact your workspace administrator to request access.
breaker.loadMissingTitle: This agent is not in the register
breaker.loadMissingBody: It may have been deleted while this page was open. Go back to the agent register to check.
breaker.closePrompt: The agent can call tools again as soon as this is saved. Your name and the reason you pick are written to the audit trail, and nothing closes a breaker automatically — this is the only thing that lets the agent act again.
breaker.reasonAcceptedTitle: I changed this agent on purpose — accept the new behaviour
breaker.reasonAcceptedBody: Discards the recorded history and starts a new baseline from now. The breaker judges nothing about this agent until it has collected {windows} active windows and {observations} tool calls again. Pick this only when the anomaly was your own change.
breaker.reasonResolvedTitle: I fixed the agent — keep the existing baseline
breaker.reasonResolvedBody: Keeps the history the agent was measured against and clears the streak. Pick this whenever the anomaly was the problem rather than the plan — re-baselining here would adopt the rogue behaviour as normal.
breaker.reasonUnknownBody: This build has no description for this reason. Do not pick it without checking what it does to the baseline.
breaker.rebaselineWarningTitle: This discards history and cannot be undone
breaker.rebaselineWarning: The {count} windows that currently count toward this agent's baseline stop counting, and the breaker reports no baseline until it has {windows} active windows and {observations} tool calls again. There is no way to bring the old baseline back.
breaker.closeErrorMissing: This agent has no breaker record, so there was nothing to close. The panel has been refreshed.

okta.description: Sync the Okta directory and verify MFA enrolment, dormant admins, admin count, and SSO federation.
okta.setupGuide: Create an API token in Okta (Security → API → Tokens) scoped to a read-only admin, and paste it below with your org URL (https://your-org.okta.com). Test connection performs a live directory ping. This connector runs directory/posture checks — it is separate from Okta SSO login.

dormantDays.description: Admin considered dormant after this many days idle (default 90).

enrichPerUser.label: Per-user MFA + admin enrichment
enrichPerUser.description: Fetch each user’s factors + roles so MFA / admin checks measure real signals. Disable on very large directories (default on).

google-workspace.description: Sync the Google Workspace directory and verify 2-Step Verification, dormant admins, admin count, and SSO.
google-workspace.setupGuide: Create a service account, enable domain-wide delegation, and authorise its client ID in the Admin console for the Directory + (optional) inbound-SSO read-only scopes. Paste the whole service-account key JSON below and the super-admin it impersonates above. Test connection performs a live token exchange and directory read, so it fails if the delegation has been revoked or the scopes are not authorised.

adminEmail.label: Admin to impersonate
adminEmail.description: A super-admin the service account impersonates via domain-wide delegation.

dormantDays.label: Dormant admin threshold (days)
dormantDays.description: Admin considered dormant after this many days idle (default 90).

enrichSso.label: SAML SSO enrichment
enrichSso.description: Read inbound SAML assignments so the SSO check reflects real coverage (default on; needs the cloud-identity.inboundsso.readonly scope).

serviceAccountJson.label: Service-account JSON
serviceAccountJson.description: A domain-wide-delegated service-account key (JSON) — paste the whole file.

entra-id.description: Sync the Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) directory — including on-prem AD identities synced via Azure AD Connect — and verify MFA registration, dormant admins, admin count, and SSO federation.
entra-id.setupGuide: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, register an application and grant it the application (not delegated) Microsoft Graph permissions User.Read.All, Directory.Read.All, and AuditLog.Read.All (the last enables MFA-registration + last-sign-in signals; without it those checks report Not applicable). Create a client secret, then paste the Directory (tenant) ID and Application (client) ID below with the secret. Test connection performs a live directory ping. On-prem Active Directory synced to Entra via Azure AD Connect is READ here for posture checks, but accounts mastered on-prem cannot be disabled through Graph — those writes are reverted by the next sync cycle, so offboarding them needs the separate on-prem Active Directory (LDAPS) connector. This connector runs directory/posture checks; it is separate from Entra SSO login. If you also want leaver offboarding to DISABLE accounts here, turn on "Allow offboarding writes" and grant the application permission User.EnableDisableAccount.All — none of the three read permissions above permits a write, Directory.Read.All included, and client-credentials tokens carry exactly what an administrator has already consented, so an existing connection keeps failing every disable until that consent is granted. If you want joiner onboarding to CREATE accounts here, turn on "Allow joiner credential issuance" and grant User.ReadWrite.All and Policy.Read.All: the joining credential is a Temporary Access Pass, which is governed by the authentication-methods policy and cannot be minted without reading it. The two switches are separate and neither implies the other — consenting the permissions alone changes nothing until the matching switch is on.

dormantDays.label: Dormant admin threshold (days)
dormantDays.description: Admin considered dormant after this many days idle (default 90).

enrichMfa.label: MFA registration enrichment
enrichMfa.description: Read the authentication-methods registration report so the MFA check reflects real enrolment (default on; needs AuditLog.Read.All).

enrichFederation.label: SSO federation enrichment
enrichFederation.description: Derive per-user SSO from each domain’s authentication type so the SSO check reflects real federation (default on).

writesEnabled.label: Allow offboarding writes
writesEnabled.description: Let leaver offboarding DISABLE accounts in this directory. Off by default. Additionally requires an administrator to consent the application permission User.EnableDisableAccount.All — the three read permissions above do not permit a write.

joinerWritesEnabled.label: Allow joiner credential issuance
joinerWritesEnabled.description: Let joiner onboarding CREATE accounts here and mint their first credential as a Temporary Access Pass. Off by default. Additionally requires an administrator to consent the application permissions User.ReadWrite.All (to create) and Policy.Read.All (a Temporary Access Pass is governed by the authentication-methods policy, which cannot be minted without reading it). Never a password and never a password fallback: if Temporary Access Pass is disabled by policy the pass refuses, because a silent downgrade is a different security posture from the one you configured.

clientSecret.label: Client secret
clientSecret.description: A client secret for the app registration.

active-directory.description: Bind to an on-premises Active Directory domain controller over LDAPS and verify dormant admins and admin count. For MFA / SSO posture on AD, use the Microsoft Entra ID connector.
active-directory.setupGuide: Provide an LDAPS URL for a reachable domain controller (ldaps://dc.corp.example.com:636), the search base DN (DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com), and a read-only service-account bind DN + password. The app must be able to reach the DC over TLS (public LDAPS or a VPN/tunnel). On-prem AD exposes no MFA or SSO-federation attribute, so those two checks report Not applicable — use the Entra ID connector for MFA/SSO posture. If your AD is synced to Entra via Azure AD Connect, prefer the Entra ID connector instead.

baseDN.label: Base DN
baseDN.description: Search base for the user enumeration.

adminGroups.label: Admin groups
adminGroups.description: Comma-separated group names treated as admin (default: Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Administrators, Schema Admins). Direct membership only.

dormantDays.label: Dormant admin threshold (days)
dormantDays.description: Admin considered dormant after this many days idle (default 90).

allowSelfSignedTls.label: Allow self-signed TLS
allowSelfSignedTls.description: Skip TLS certificate verification for an internal/enterprise CA (default off — verification on).

writesEnabled.label: Allow offboarding writes
writesEnabled.description: Let leaver offboarding DISABLE accounts in this directory. Off by default: connecting a directory grants reading only, and this is the separate, per-connection decision that it may also be written to. It does NOT permit creating accounts.

createOU.label: Creation OU
createOU.description: Where a joiner create lands. Must sit under the base DN above — an account created outside that scope cannot be found by the leaver pass, so it could be provisioned and never offboarded. Leave empty and creates are refused.

bindDN.label: Bind DN (service account)
bindDN.description: A read-only service account DN or userPrincipalName, e.g. CN=svc-inflect,OU=Service,DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com.

bindPassword.label: Bind password
bindPassword.description: Password for the bind service account.

writeBindDN.label: Write bind DN (optional)
writeBindDN.description: Separate service account used only for offboarding writes. Needs Write permission on the userAccountControl property of user objects, delegated at the OU holding them — NOT Account Operators and NOT Domain Admins. Leave blank to reuse the read bind.

writeBindPassword.label: Write bind password (optional)
writeBindPassword.description: Password for the write service account. Required if a write bind DN is set.

legacy-mcp.description: A read-only view of a legacy application's access tables, exposed through a tool server the customer runs in front of it. Connecting one does not recertify anything: the accounts it exposes are reconciled against HR and a person confirms every link.
legacy-mcp.setupGuide: Enter the HTTPS endpoint of the tool server you run in front of the legacy application, and the bearer token it expects. Testing the connection performs a real handshake and reads the manifest, which tells you whether the server speaks the inflect-legacy-access/1 contract. The endpoint must be reachable on a public address over HTTPS: private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused, redirects are not followed, and changing the endpoint later requires re-entering the token.

endpointUrl.label: Tool server URL
endpointUrl.description: HTTPS endpoint of your tool server, e.g. https://legacy-tools.example.com/rpc

applicationName.label: Application name
applicationName.description: What to call this application in reviews and findings. Defaults to the name the server reports in its manifest.

bearerToken.label: Bearer token
bearerToken.description: Sent as an Authorization: Bearer header. It is encrypted at rest and is never returned by the API, shown in a validation message, written to a log line or recorded in an audit row.

workday.description: Sync the worker roster from Workday into the personnel hub.
workday.setupGuide: In Workday, register an API Client for Integrations with the Staffing scope and a redirect URI, then publish the Inflect roster report as a RaaS custom report. Provide the tenant host, tenant name, report path, and the client id + secret. Test connection performs a real token exchange against your tenant.

clientSecret.label: API client secret
clientSecret.description: The secret from the Workday API Client for Integrations.

orangehrm.description: An OrangeHRM directory, read for the HRIS roster. Supports the OAuth2 client-credentials grant against an instance on a host covered by ORANGEHRM_HOSTS.
orangehrm.setupGuide: Stand up an OrangeHRM instance on a host covered by ORANGEHRM_HOSTS, register an API client for the OAuth2 client-credentials grant, and provide the instance URL with the client id and secret. Test connection performs a real token exchange against the instance.

writeBackEnabled.label: Allow HRIS write-back
writeBackEnabled.description: Let the JML write-back preflight use this connection. Off by default, and separate from directory write consent. No HRIS write exists yet — turning this on permits a read-only check that the stored credential can reach the record and the field a future write would target.

clientSecret.label: API client secret
clientSecret.description: The secret from the OrangeHRM API client.

device.description: Internal checks over the device inventory: disk encryption, screen lock, antivirus, password manager.

training.description: Internal checks over security-awareness training completion and background-check status.

servicenow.description: Change-management evidence from ServiceNow — approvals on production changes.
servicenow.setupGuide: Create a dedicated ServiceNow integration user with read access to the change_request table (a scoped read-only role is enough — this connection never writes). Provide the instance host, the table, and how far back each run should look. Test connection performs a real authenticated read of that table, so an integration user without an ACL on it is reported at setup rather than at 05:00.

windowDays.label: Look-back window (days)
windowDays.description: How far back each run reads. Should be at least as long as the control period.

password.label: Integration user password
password.description: The password for the dedicated read-only integration user.

mcp-server.description: An external Model Context Protocol server an agent can be granted tools on. Connecting one does not grant anything: its tools must be reviewed and pinned, then granted to a specific registered agent, before any run can call them.
mcp-server.setupGuide: Enter the server's HTTPS endpoint, then choose how it authenticates. A server behind Microsoft Entra takes the tenant ID, client ID and client secret, plus EITHER a refresh token (delegated — every token carries a named person's privileges, so an agent can never see more than that person) OR a token scope (app-only — no such ceiling, and the scope must name your server's own audience). Anything else takes a static Authorization header value, which works but expires with the token you paste. Testing the connection performs a real handshake with the tool server and reports how many tools it advertises. Those tools are NOT usable yet: an administrator reviews and approves them, and they must then be granted to a registered agent. The server must be reachable on a public address over HTTPS — private and link-local addresses are refused, and redirects are not followed.

url.label: Server URL
url.description: HTTPS endpoint of the tool server, e.g. https://tools.example.com/rpc

tenantId.label: Entra tenant ID
tenantId.description: For a server behind Microsoft Entra. Leave blank for a server that takes a static credential.

clientId.label: Application (client) ID
clientId.description: The app registration authorized against this tool server.

scope.label: Token scope (audience)
scope.description: The resource this server's token is for, e.g. https://tools.example.com/.default. REQUIRED for app-only access (client secret, no refresh token) — there is no safe default, because a token minted for the wrong audience is refused as an invalid token rather than as a bad secret. Optional for delegated access, which defaults to the tool-server resource Microsoft Entra provides.

authorization.label: Authorization header
authorization.description: Sent verbatim as the Authorization header, e.g. "Bearer …". Leave blank for a server that needs no credential, or use the Entra fields below — a pasted token expires and the connection stops working with it.

clientSecret.label: Client secret
clientSecret.description: The app registration's secret. Required with the Entra fields.

refreshToken.label: Refresh token
refreshToken.description: Obtained once, interactively. Exchanged for a short-lived access token on demand, so the connection keeps working — the access token is never stored. Supplying it selects DELEGATED access, where every token carries a named person's privileges and an agent can never see more than that person. Leave it blank, with a scope set, for APP-ONLY access, which has no such ceiling.

a2a-peer.description: The route an agent's task to a registered A2A peer agent is sent through. Connecting one grants nothing: the send is offered to an agent only once it is granted the tool, this connection is above DISABLED on the external write ladder, and the peer's agent card is pinned by a person and still matches its pin.
a2a-peer.setupGuide: Register and pin the peer first, under Agents → Peers. Then name it here by its peer id. If the peer issued Inflect a credential, paste it as the Authorization header value (for example "Bearer …"); it is encrypted at rest and sent only to the endpoint in that peer's pinned card. The connection starts at DISABLED on the external write ladder and is widened one rung at a time by an owner.

peerId.label: Peer id
peerId.description: The id of the registered A2A peer this connection sends to.

authorization.label: Authorization header
authorization.description: The credential the peer issued this workspace, sent verbatim as the Authorization header. Leave blank for a peer that relies on signatures alone.

pullReason.AUTHENTICATION_FAILED: The application's server refused the saved token. Update the token on this connection.
pullReason.SSRF_BLOCKED: The application's address is not one this service may call.
pullReason.TIMEOUT: The application's server did not answer in time.
pullReason.CONTRACT_VIOLATION: The application's server answered in a form this connection does not accept.
pullReason.CAP_EXCEEDED: The read was cut short at its limit, so it does not hold the whole table. Check that the connection points at an access table.
pullReason.TORN_SNAPSHOT: The table changed while it was being read, so its pages do not come from one copy. Read the accounts again.
pullReason.INCOMPLETE_READ: The read did not cover every page the server said it had.
pullReason.SCHEMA_DRIFT: The application's columns changed after the column mapping was saved. Read the columns and save the mapping again.
pullReason.AMBIGUOUS_COLUMN_CASE: Two columns differ only in upper and lower case, so they cannot be told apart.
pullReason.MISSING_ACCOUNT_KEY: Some rows have no value in the column mapped to the account key.
pullReason.DUPLICATE_ACCOUNT_KEY: One account appears on more than one row, and the saved layout does not allow that.
pullReason.CONTRADICTORY_ROWS: One account appears on several rows that disagree with each other.
pullReason.SECRET_SHAPED_VALUE: A mapped value looks like a password or a key, so nothing from this read was kept. Map that column differently, or leave it out at the source.
pullReason.ROW_SCHEMA_INVALID: A row holds values the account fields do not accept.
pullReason.MAPPING_MISSING: No column mapping is saved for this connection.

leaverPasses.title: Leaver passes
leaverPasses.intro: Every offboarding pass this tenant has run, most recent first. What a pass was allowed to do depends on the write mode it ran under — each pass states its own, and the setting in force now is named below. This is the record the observation window exists to be compared against: read each pass beside what HR and IT actually did before this tenant is widened another rung.

leaverPasses.syncStaleHeading: The directory sync, not the rails, is why these accounts were not disabled
leaverPasses.syncStaleBody: {count} of this pass’s decisions were refused because the account’s on-premises state was last observed too long ago to act on. Those accounts were NOT disabled, and re-running the pass will not change that — what is being refused is the AGE of the observation, not the account. The usual cause is that the connection which observes these accounts has been disabled, so no sync refreshes them any more: re-enable it, or remove the accounts it left behind.
leaverPasses.syncNeverObservedHeading: No sync has ever observed these accounts
leaverPasses.syncNeverObservedBody: {count} of this pass’s decisions were refused because no sync has ever recorded whether the account is mastered on-premises, and unknown is not the same as cloud-only. Those accounts were NOT disabled. One successful directory sync clears this; if it is still here after the next 03:00 run, the sync is not reaching these accounts.

leaverPasses.emptyOverdueDescription: Leaver writes are switched on and a pass should already have run at 05:00 UTC. A pass records a row even when it refuses, so an empty page here points at the directory connection or the background worker rather than at this setting.
leaverPasses.forbidden: Reading which accounts a leaver pass would have disabled requires tenant-owner access.
leaverPasses.unsettledHeading: Directory writes from an earlier pass were never confirmed
leaverPasses.unsettledBody: When this pass started, {count} write(s) against this directory had been waiting over an hour with no outcome recorded. Each one captured the account’s state BEFORE the change, so the account may or may not have been altered — the only way to settle it is to read the account in the directory itself and compare. These are not decisions this pass made, and re-running it will not clear them.
leaverPasses.unsettledUnknownHeading: The unconfirmed-write backlog could not be read
leaverPasses.unsettledUnknownBody: This pass could not count the directory writes still waiting for an outcome, so this report cannot say whether there are any. That is not the same as none. Nothing was stopped — the read is deliberately allowed to fail rather than end an offboarding — but treat the figure as unknown, not as zero.
leaverPasses.noProtectedHeading: No account here is marked protected
leaverPasses.noProtectedBody: Leaver writes are enabled for this direction and none of the {population} active account(s) in scope is marked protected. The account this integration signs in as is still protected automatically — that rail is separate and always on. Everything else is not: a break-glass account, a shared service account or a contractor identity that appears in an HR export as a leaver will be disabled by an automated pass with nothing to stop it. Mark those accounts protected on the connected accounts page before this direction runs unattended.

steps.RANSOMWARE-1: Isolate affected hosts from the network (disable NICs / segment off) — do not power down, to preserve memory.
steps.RANSOMWARE-2: Capture volatile evidence (memory, running processes) before remediation.
steps.RANSOMWARE-3: Identify the ransomware family, encrypted file extensions, and the initial access vector.
steps.RANSOMWARE-4: Verify integrity and isolation of backups (confirm they are offline / immutable and unaffected).
steps.RANSOMWARE-5: Revoke and rotate credentials that may have been exposed; disable compromised accounts.
steps.RANSOMWARE-6: Engage your incident-response retainer / national CSIRT; do not pay or negotiate without legal + executive sign-off.
steps.DATA_BREACH-1: Determine the data categories, volume, and subjects affected (scope the exposure).
steps.DATA_BREACH-2: Stop the exfiltration path — revoke tokens/keys, close the exposed endpoint, block the egress.
steps.DATA_BREACH-3: Reset credentials and invalidate sessions for affected accounts.
steps.DATA_BREACH-4: Preserve access logs and the exposure timeline as evidence.
steps.DATA_BREACH-5: Assess GDPR Art. 33/34 obligations with the DPO (personal-data breach notification may apply in parallel to NIS2 Art. 23).
steps.DATA_BREACH-6: Monitor affected accounts/systems for follow-on fraudulent activity.
steps.DDOS-1: Characterise the attack (volumetric / protocol / application-layer) and identify targeted services.
steps.DDOS-2: Engage upstream DDoS mitigation / scrubbing (provider, CDN, or WAF rate-limiting).
steps.DDOS-3: Apply rate limits, geo/IP filtering, and drop known-bad traffic at the edge.
steps.DDOS-4: Scale or fail over critical services; protect the origin behind the mitigation layer.

steps.UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS-3: Determine lateral movement and what data/systems the actor reached.
steps.UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS-4: Rotate secrets the actor could have accessed; enforce MFA re-enrolment.

steps.UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS-6: Review and tighten access controls / privileged-access paths exploited.

orphanPass.accessMessage: Only an owner can view or change the owner-orphan pass. Its mode decides whether a nightly job stops agents whose owner has left.
orphanPass.title: Owner departures
orphanPass.intro: Every night at 05:15 UTC, the owner-orphan pass looks for active agents whose accountable owner has left this workspace: no active membership, or an HR record marked terminated. Its mode decides what it does about them.
orphanPass.blurb: Off checks nothing. Dry run records each orphan and tells the owners, and changes nothing. Automatic engages each orphan's kill switch, suspends it, and asks for its Entra service principal to be disabled through the external write ladder.

confirmBody.DRY_RUN: From the next pass, each orphan is recorded and every owner is told. Nothing is stopped. The pass must stay here seven days, with at least one recorded pass, before it can widen.
confirmBody.AUTOMATIC: From the next pass, each orphan's kill switch is engaged and the agent is suspended, by the system, with nobody approving it. Only the agent's new owner can lift that kill, after an ownership transfer completes.
